summary: Destiny entries from the prepared 1000-title candidate queue, researched for Sami's fidelity-first archive route.

entries.title: Destiny
entries.definitive_edition: Destiny: The Collection on PS4/PS5 or Xbox One/Series backward compatibility

emulation.notes: Use supported console/backward-compatible route; no PC version exists.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PS4/Xbox One version with all expansions installed

primary.version: Destiny: The Collection on current backward-compatible console route
primary.why: Destiny 1 was never released on PC, and Bungie's own support guidance treats PS4/Xbox One as the full Rise of Iron-era route while PS3/Xbox 360 are capped at The Taken King-era legacy content. The Collection is the cleanest content-complete route, but server/account state and player population must be logged.
primary.how_to_play: Use Destiny: The Collection on PS4/PS5 backward compatibility or Xbox One/Series backward compatibility. Record platform, patch, account, expansions installed, online service status, matchmaking/raid-fireteam state, character boost use, and any legacy-console comparison.

secondary.exclusive_content: Legacy-console state capped before Rise of Iron
secondary.what_to_play: Use only if documenting the legacy-console branch.
secondary.why: Bungie support separates legacy-console content from the PS4/Xbox One full route.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record online-service status, expansion ownership, account progression, fireteam availability, and legacy-console limits.

entries.title: Destiny 2
entries.definitive_edition: Current PC client after Update 9.7.0, with content/account/server state documented

emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Current official service state after final live-service update

primary.why: Destiny 2 is now a post-active-development live-service archive target: Bungie released the final live-service content update on June 9, 2026 while keeping the game playable. The current route must document available content, vaulted content limitations, account state, expansion ownership, and server/update status.
primary.how_to_play: Use the current PC client through Steam/Epic/Microsoft/Bungie. Record update/build, server status, account, expansion/content ownership, Guardian class/power, available campaigns/activities, vaulted-content limitations, fireteam/solo state, and any post-final-update hotfixes.

secondary.why: PC is the best capture route, but cross-save/account state can matter.

secondary.what_to_play: Document from historical sources only unless preserved access exists.
secondary.why: The current client no longer represents the full launch content state.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record available content, vaulted-content limitations, expansion ownership, account state, and post-final-update hotfixes.
